revised_boundary.caveat: An extrapolation from one point along a theoretical slope, not a series of runs. The two wide-base rungs measured here (75.2 at 45 bits, 61.2 at 48) fall more slowly than that slope, which would put the boundary further out; the slope is used because it is the one the cost laws predict.
revised_boundary.method: the charged ratio falls as the square root of r, so 48 + 2*log2(ratio)

against_the_projection.what_was_projected: docs/ic/runs/koblitz-degree53-and-reach-20260912.json put the charged ratio at 5.1 at 48 bits and said the whole-process class would need about 315 targets there.
against_the_projection.why_it_under_predicted: The projection used the constants of a 15264-point base with a full scan. Since then collection reached its 2r/|F|^2 floor, two setup costs left the precompute, and the compact pair table more than doubled the base. Each moved a constant the projection had fixed.

comparison_with_degree_53.note: rho grew 2.65 times against a square-root prediction of 2.78, and the descent 3.3 times against a probe-count prediction of 6.5 -- the degree-61 probes were about twice as cheap each, on a base with 296 columns against 344.

what_this_is: K_0 over F_2^61 has a 48-bit prime-order subgroup, the largest this curve family offers inside single-word arithmetic, and 7.7 times the degree-53 rung. Run end to end on a 36112-point compact-table base against the signed-Frobenius rho baseline.
what_this_is_not: Not an attack on a curve in use: a 48-bit subgroup is far below any deployed parameter.
Not a claim that the exponent moved: the descent still costs 2r/|F|^2 probes.
Not a distributed or multi-machine measurement: one process, four cores.
The revised boundary is an extrapolation from measured constants, not a measured boundary.
